issues.issue: "Originator" is defined only "[a]s defined in the Recitals," where it means the "various originators" from which the Seller bought loans, so an operative defined term is supplied by a recital rather than by the body. Exhibit C names only six such originators, which does not obviously match "various originators."

The definition reads "the absolute maximum amount by which the Mortgage Interest Rate there may increase or decrease," a garbled phrase, and it duplicates the separately defined "Mortgage Interest Rate Cap." It also fixes the cap by what is "set forth as such on the Mortgage Loan Schedule" with no rule if the Note differs.

The "applicable" Prior Purchase Agreement is to be found on Exhibit C, but Exhibit C lists several successive amended and restated agreements per originator against multiple purchase dates without stating which governs a given loan. Which agreement's warranties were assigned for a particular loan is not determinable from the exhibit.

The Purchase Price Percentage — the operative price term, and a component of the Repurchase Price — is fixed only by the Letter Agreement between Morgan Stanley & Co. Incorporated and Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc., neither of which is a party to this agreement and which is not attached. The price cannot be determined from the instrument.

A Qualified Appraiser must have been "duly appointed by the Seller," although the recitals state that the Seller purchased the Mortgage Loans from various Originators who arranged the appraisals at origination. The requirement cannot be satisfied as written for loans the Seller did not originate.

"Qualified Correspondent" is defined at length, together with "Designated Guidelines," but neither term is used in any operative provision or in Exhibit F. The definition has no work to do, raising the question whether a qualification meant to condition the representations was dropped.

Clause (ii) requires a Mortgage Interest Rate "not less than and not more than 1% greater than" that of the Deleted Mortgage Loan, an incomplete comparative that omits what the rate must not be less than, and clause (iii) uses the same construction for term to maturity. The eligibility test cannot be applied as written.

The definition allows successors "designated by the Purchasers," a plural referring to a party this agreement defines in the singular, leaving unclear who may designate a replacement agency. The term is also used only in Exhibit F's hazard-insurance representation, in the plural form "Rating Agencies."

Regulation AB is incorporated "as amended from time to time" and as subject to whatever clarification the Commission or its staff "may" later provide, so the Seller's Section 12 disclosure obligations can change after signing. The content of the obligation is not fixed by the instrument.

"Representations and Warranties" is defined in Subsection 8.02 to mean the representations of the related Originator under the Prior Purchase Agreements, yet the cure and repurchase paragraphs of Subsection 8.02 use the same defined term in a way that appears to reach the Seller's own Exhibit F representations. Which set of warranties triggers the repurchase machinery turns on this definition.

The Repurchase Price is built on the "Purchase Price Percentage," which is fixed only in a Letter Agreement between two non-parties and is not attached, so the repurchase amount cannot be computed from this instrument. It also differs from the 100% par-plus-interest "Purchase Price" the securitization documents use for the same loans.

The list ends "(vi) a Manufactured Home, none of which is a mobile home," and it is unclear whether the qualifier attaches only to Manufactured Homes or to all six categories. The distinction between a manufactured home and a mobile home is also left undefined.

"Second Lien Loan" presupposes a Mortgage creating a second lien, but the "Mortgage" definition in this same section describes an instrument "which creates a first lien on the Mortgaged Property." The two definitions cannot both be given effect.

The Servicer is "the Servicer set forth on Exhibit B," but Exhibit B as attached says only "Provided Upon Request," while Section 7 speaks of the Servicing Agreements "set forth on Exhibit C." Which exhibit identifies the servicer for a given loan is unresolved.

Servicing Rights are reserved to the Seller under Subsection 6.01 and include "any and all documents, files, records, servicing files ... or other information pertaining to the Mortgage Loans," which overlaps the Mortgage Files that Subsection 6.01 conveys to the Purchaser. Which party is entitled to the overlapping files cannot be settled from the two provisions.

Clause (i) is "the principal balance of such Mortgage Loan at the Cut-off Date after giving effect to payments of principal due on or before such date," where "such date" could mean the Cut-off Date or the date of determination in the opening words. The choice changes the balance on which the Purchase Price and Repurchase Price are computed.

The quantity purchased is an aggregate Stated Principal Balance "in an amount set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule," but the Schedule attached as Exhibit B states only "Provided Upon Request." How much was agreed to be bought cannot be determined from the instrument.

The Schedule must be delivered at least two Business Days before the May 31, 2007 Closing Date, yet the Schedule's own definition requires balances, rates and payment data "as of the Cut-off Date" of June 1, 2007 — data that cannot exist when delivery is due. The two dates cannot be worked together.

The price is the Purchase Price Percentage times the aggregate Stated Principal Balance "after application of payments of principal due or received on or before the Cut-off Date," although the Stated Principal Balance definition already gives effect to principal due on or before that date. Read literally the deduction is taken twice.

The Purchaser takes principal from the Cut-off Date (June 1, 2007) but interest only "from and after the Closing Date" (May 31, 2007), so the two entitlements are measured from different dates, and the same section's price is computed as of the Cut-off Date. Who owns interest accruing between the two dates is left unresolved.

The examination right runs through "the applicable Custodian (as set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit B hereto)," but Exhibit B is not attached in substance ("Provided Upon Request") and identifies no custodian. The mechanics of the pre-closing review cannot be carried out from the document.

This subsection assigns the Prior Purchase Agreements "except with respect to the Group 1 Mortgage Loans," while Subsection 8.02 states flatly that the Purchaser "shall be the assignee of the representations and warranties of the related Originator ... as described in Subsection 6.01" without that carve-out. Whether the Purchaser holds Originator warranties for Group 1 loans is contestable.

Record title is to remain "in the name of the Seller or an Affiliate of the Seller" while ownership is "vested solely in the Purchaser," and all funds received after the Cut-off Date belong to the Purchaser even though Section 4 gives the Purchaser interest only from the Closing Date. The provisions pull in different directions on both title and cash.

The paragraph breaks off mid-sentence ("and a asa a sale of assets 0 on the"), so the corresponding accounting and tax treatment required of the Seller is missing from the text. What the parties agreed about the Seller's books cannot be read from the provision.

Subsection 8.02 requires substitute loans to be delivered "with the Mortgage Note endorsed as required by Subsection 6.03," but this subsection imposes no endorsement requirement at all — endorsement appears only in Exhibit A-1. The delivery standard invoked elsewhere is absent here.

The loans are said to be sold "on a servicing retained basis," yet Subsection 6.01 reserves the Servicing Rights to the Seller while the next paragraph of this section assigns each Servicing Agreement to the Purchaser and has the Servicer service "for the Purchaser." Who holds the servicing after closing cannot be squared across the three provisions.

The servicing arrangements are to be "as set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit C hereto," but the Mortgage Loan Schedule is Exhibit B and Exhibit C contains the Prior Purchase Agreements and Servicing Agreements tables. The cross-reference points to the wrong exhibit.

Servicing of the Non-transferred Loans is to move to Saxon on "the related Servicing Transfer Dates set forth on Exhibit E," two of which (July 2, 2007) fall after the Closing Date and after the loans have been on-sold, and the exhibit's stated amounts exceed the pool being sold. How the transfer obligation operates post-sale is unaddressed.

The sentence contains the phrase "is required" twice ("No consent ... is required for the transactions ... having jurisdiction over the Seller is required or, if required ..."), leaving the representation ungrammatical. Whether it warrants that no consent is needed, or only that any needed consent has been obtained, is unclear.

The no-conflicts representation is limited to breaches of "the Seller's charter or by-laws," omitting any warranty against conflict with law or with other agreements binding the Seller. Whether that omission was deliberate limits what the Purchaser can claim.

The representation is that the Seller "does not believe, nor does it have any reason or cause to believe, that it cannot perform," a purely subjective formulation with no objective benchmark. What state of knowledge breaches it is not ascertainable.

This paragraph states that the Purchaser is assignee of the Originators' representations "as described in Subsection 6.01," but Subsection 6.01 excludes the Group 1 Mortgage Loans from the assignment of the Prior Purchase Agreements. It also fixes the defined term "Representations and Warranties" as the Originators' warranties only, which the later remedy paragraphs appear to use more broadly.

The Seller's own Exhibit F warranties are made here, but the repurchase machinery in the following paragraphs is triggered by breach of a "Representation and Warranty" — a term the preceding paragraph defines as the Originators' warranties under the Prior Purchase Agreements. Whether the Seller's Exhibit F warranties carry the repurchase remedy is therefore in doubt.

The trigger is the breach of "a Representation and Warranty," the defined term meaning the Originators' warranties under the Prior Purchase Agreements, even though condition (2) then addresses what the Originator has failed to do and Exhibit F contains the Seller's own warranties. Which warranties set the 120-day clock running cannot be settled from the paragraph.

The paragraph says that "within 120 days ... the Seller shall take such actions as described in the following paragraph," while the following paragraph independently allows 120 days from discovery or notice to cure before repurchase is required. Whether the 120 days is one period or two consecutive ones is unclear.

The substitution alternative applies where the Seller learns of the breach "within 180 days of the Closing Date" but requires the substitution to be "effected not later than 180 days after the Closing Date," so a breach discovered near day 180 leaves no time to substitute, and the 120-day cure period in the second sentence can outrun the substitution window. The remedies cannot be sequenced as written.

Substitution must be effected by delivering "the documents required by Subsection 6.03, with the Mortgage Note endorsed as required by Subsection 6.03," but Subsection 6.03 requires only custodial certifications and imposes no endorsement requirement, which appears instead in Exhibit A-1. The delivery obligation invokes a standard the cited subsection does not contain.
